newsitem.title: JAPAN: Flu death toll among Japan's elderly rises to 249.
newsitem.headline: Flu death toll among Japan's elderly rises to 249.

text.p: An influenza virus sweeping through homes for the elderly in Japan has killed 249 people in the past month, Japan's Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper reported on Sunday.
The virus has ravaged nursing homes and other welfare facilities throughout Japan since late December, according to a survey conducted by Yomiuri.

The deaths were concentrated in northeastern Japan, particularly Aomori, Iwate, Akita and Miyagi prefectures. The flu virus also has appeared in 13 prefectures in southwestern Japan but no cases of flu-related deaths have yet been reported, Yomiuri said.
The Hong Kong A flu strain raging through Japan was recently joined by the type B virus, which is considered less contagious and carries lighter symptoms than type A, health officials said.
The flu is commonly followed by pneumonia in the elderly, who are more prone to infections, and health authorities warned welfare facilities to watch for early flu signs among those in their care.

The seasonal increase in flu cases in late December was the highest on record, health officials said. The last flu epidemic in 1994-95 claimed 1,244 lives nationwide, mostly among the elderly, according to the Health Ministry.
